newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail freight traffic up from year ago -- AAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail freight traffic up from year ago -- AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic was up 3.1 percent in the latest week from a year ago, fueled by a rise in chemical and coal carloadings, and in trailer and container movement, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
The AAR said it estimated total railroad volume in the week ended December 7 at 26.5 billion ton-miles, up 3.1 percent from 25.7 a year ago. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
"This past week's increase was fueled primarily by gains in chemicals, coal and intermodal (trailers and containers)," AAR chief economist Harvey Levine said in a release.

Freight traffic on major railroads in the latest week included new carloadings of 353,297, up 1.4 percent from 348,510 a year ago. New traffic in trailers and containers totalled 165,297, up 5.3 percent from 157,037 in the year-ago week.
Carloadings were down in 10 categories from a year ago, and up in nine categories.
"Chemical loadings were especially strong, showing an increase of more than 3,000 cars. Coal was up more than 5,000 cars," Levine said.
So far this year, the AAR said carloadings were down 0.5 percent from the same period last year, trailer and container traffic was up 2.0 percent, and ton-miles were up 1.9 percent.
